overview: Cape Verde, also called Cabo Verde, is an island country in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Praia, on the island of Santiago. The islands were uninhabited until the Portuguese arrived in the 1400s, and Cape Verde became independent from Portugal in 1975. It is known for morna music, made famous by the singer Cesária Évora.

geography.text: Cape Verde is made up of ten volcanic islands, nine of them inhabited. Some, such as Fogo with its still-active volcano, are mountainous, while others are flat and sandy. The climate is dry, and droughts have often been a problem.

history.text: Cabo Verde's islands were uninhabited when Portuguese sailors found them around 1456. They became a stop on the Atlantic slave trade, and a Creole culture grew there. Cabo Verde won independence together with Guinea-Bissau's liberation movement and became independent in 1975. It is now one of Africa's most stable democracies.

events.title: Islands discovered
events.text: Portuguese sailors reach the uninhabited islands.

events.title: First settlement
events.text: Ribeira Grande is founded, the first European town in the tropics.

events.title: PAIGC founded
events.text: Amílcar Cabral founds a movement to free Guinea-Bissau and Cabo Verde.

events.title: Democracy
events.text: The first multi-party elections are held.
